text:
marta: seeing intermittent token stalls on streaming endpoints from a subset of hosts in us-west-2c. spikes line up with gRPC deadline hits on consumer side.
infra-bot: alert: increase in gRPC deadline_exceeded for service=stream-gen region=us-west-2c hosts=pool-gpu-7x.* count=42
oliver: which hosts? any recent infra changes in that AZ?
marta: hosts: pool-gpu-7x-23, -24, -27. no config changes scheduled. kube node upgrades last week but those were rolled back.
ram: can you paste a tcpdump from a problematic host? look for out-of-order sequences / SACKs.
marta: dropping a small snippet, captured with `tcpdump -i eth0 -w reorder.pcap` and `tcpdump -r reorder.pcap -nn -ttt 'tcp' | head -n 40`:
```
12:00:01.123456 IP 10.10.3.27.50234 > 10.10.4.2.443: Flags [P.], seq 1201:1601, ack 2101, win 229, length 400
12:00:01.123457 IP 10.10.4.2.443 > 10.10.3.27.50234: Flags [.], ack 1601, win 512, length 0
12:00:01.123458 IP 10.10.3.27.50234 > 10.10.4.2.443: Flags [P.], seq 1601:2001, ack 2101, length 400
12:00:01.123459 IP 10.10.4.2.443 > 10.10.3.27.50234: Flags [.], ack 1201, win 512, length 0  # <-- ack for older seq (reordered)
12:00:01.123460 IP 10.10.4.2.443 > 10.10.3.27.50234: Flags [.], ack 2001, win 512, length 0
12:00:01.123462 IP 10.10.3.27.50234 > 10.10.4.2.443: Flags [P.], seq 2001:2401, ack 2101, length 400
12:00:01.123463 IP 10.10.4.2.443 > 10.10.3.27.50234: Flags [.], ack 1601, win 512, length 0  # repeated SACK/dup acks
```

maya: those dup acks and non-monotonic ack numbers smell like reordering at L2/L3 or NIC offload. do we see any SACK options?
marta: tcpdump shows SACK blocks in options on the ACKs.
ram: likely causes: ECMP hashing sending packets across different spine paths with variable latency, gre/encapsulation MTU mismatch causing fragmentation/reassembly order changes, or NIC driver/fpga bug with GRO/LRO merging.
alex: low-effort repro steps: on a repro node, try disabling GRO/LRO/GSO and see if reordering symptoms disappear. commands: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off` and then run a quick stream to the model host and check token gaps.
oliver: also try `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps=0`? not sure but keep kernel offload changes minimal.
marta: rolling a canary: will disable GRO on pool-gpu-7x-24 during low traffic window, run k6 streaming load locally and watch token inter-arrival times.
maya: if that helps, next step is to check NIC firmware + driver versions across the pool and correlate with affected hosts.
ram: also open cloud provider ticket about ECMP path symmetry and ask for per-packet reordering visibility (they have a packet-inspect service). include pcap and example flows.
alex: if firmware/driver fixes not available, mitigation options: pin flows with consistent hash (disable 5-tuple ECMP), set MTU to uniform value on all switches/hosts, or move affected nodes to a different AZ sub-pool.
oliver: can we temporarily lower gRPC stream deadlines / add client-side jitter/backoff to tolerate short reorders? risky but possible as short mitigation.
marta: canary started. initial numbers: token gap median dropped from 180ms -> 28ms after disabling GRO on test node. will keep running for 30m and collect traces.
ram: nice, suggests offload interaction. please capture ethtool -k and `dmesg` before/after.
infra-bot: ticket created: #INFRA-3245 opened with cloud provider, attached pcap and sample traces.
marta: thanks all. will update in ~40m with final canary results. :thumbsup:
oliver: thanks — if canary looks good, we schedule narrow rollback window to flip off GRO on the rest and then plan permanent fix (driver/firmware or hw migration).
marta: update: after 37m, canary stable, no more gRPC deadline_exceeded for that host. pushing a rolling mitigation to remaining 3 affected nodes now.
ram: remember to document perf delta and cost impact (cpu up from offloads). estimate +2% CPU on those nodes.
maya: noted. filing follow-ups for tracking.
alex: great triage, team. keep a note for model owners: minor client-side latency variability while we fix infra.
marta: closing thread when all nodes done.
